Helion to provide final success criteria sign-off by 2026-01-22
SE to run 1-off latency and quality benchmark for 2.7B quant model by 2026-01-20
Set follow-up executive readout on 2026-01-27 if signoff complete
action_items: Priya Nair - export token-level cost breakdown and 3 sample trace logs (due 2026-01-18)
Carlos Ruiz - confirm production traffic slice and SLA targets (due 2026-01-22)
Tara Singh - provide finance baseline for NPV calc and target TCO (due 2026-01-21)

summary: Final pilot sync to align stakeholders on measured outcomes, finalize success criteria for go/no-go, review tuning run results (latency, cost, accuracy) and agree next steps for procurement and pilot-to-prod economics. Broad alignment on using Redwood Dedicated if the cost model meets target; request for final benchmark on quantized 2.7B variant and confirmation of SSO/KMS integration timeline.
topics: commercial next steps and procurement timeline
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Think we have about 55 minutes today. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Carlos: Carlos here, sorry I'm on mobile; got the packet.
[00:10] Aisha: Aisha — Product. Good to go.
[00:12] Tara: Tara in Finance.
[00:14] Priya (SE): Priya here. Devon from SRE on the line too.
[00:18] Speaker 6: yep
[00:20] Jordan: Great. Agenda — recap the pilot readouts, make sure the success criteria map to what you measured, agree any tuning left, and decide next steps for economics and procurement. Carlos, do you want to kick off with your view of the results?
[00:35] Carlos: Sure. Overall we're happy — generation quality looked on par vs baseline for our top-50 prompts, and the feature extraction/embedding side was within expected variance. The outstanding bit for us is latency at peak; p95 is hovering around 380ms for the hosted variant and closer to 160ms on a dedicated pool with batching. We need p95 <200ms for the interactive use case.
[00:55] Priya: Right, that's consistent with the traces we saw. For the dedicated pool we enabled continuous batching and prefix caching; that dropped per-token cost by roughly 22% and p95 improved. There was some variability when the token lengths spiked above 1,000 — the kernel selection warmed up.
[01:15] Aisha: Can you unpack the cost delta? Tara's asked for an apples-to-apples on committed vs on-demand.
[01:22] Tara: yeah, please.
[01:24] Jordan: We'll send the runbook with the committed baseline. High level: hosted on our standard plan runs higher unit cost — about 35% — compared to Redwood Dedicated with reserved capacity, assuming your 99th percentile usage pattern. For the pilot numbers you shared, Dedicated looks about 28% cheaper over a 12-month projection. We'll put the exact numbers into the appendix.
[01:44] Tara: Important for finance is the break-even and the incremental uplift to revenue from faster conversion. If we go Dedicated we need a buy window of 6-9 months to justify the capex.
[01:55] Jordan: Understood. We'll model both 6- and 12-month commit curves.
[02:00] Carlos: One technical ask — can Redwood run the same workload on the 2.7B quantized model and report top-line latency + quality delta? We want to see if quantization gives us the latency headroom without regression on the prompts that matter.
[02:12] Priya: Yes — we already did a quick pass during the pilot and saw roughly 12-15% lower latency and about a 2-3% drop in exact-match on the templates that are sensitive — but that was with default quantization settings. We can re-run with the tuning settings we discussed and share traces.
[02:30] Carlos: Good, please do that.
[02:33] Devon (SRE): one note — network egress to the dedicated region might add jitter; curious if you have any samples with VPC peering on.
[02:41] Priya: We have the VPC test harness results in the repo; the extra hops added ~8–12ms median in our trial. We also saw a couple of mis-labeled headers in the traces — "K-V cash" as spelled in the auto transcript — but it's KV cache.
[02:58] Aisha: On success criteria — our product metric requires 1) p95 latency < 200ms in peak conditions, 2) inference cost per 1k generated tokens < $0.85, and 3) human-rated quality delta <= 5% vs current SOTA. Can we map those to what you measured?
[03:15] Priya: We can map. Current dedicated runs hit p95 ~160ms on median traffic, cost per 1k tokens with the recommended batching was $0.72 in the committed model, and the human eval set we ran showed a 3.8% delta at our sample size.
[03:31] Tara: Those cost figures look promising. But we need the sensitivity table — if traffic doubles, what's the per-token cost? We prefer a sliding scale.
[03:38] Jordan: We'll include a sensitivity table. The runbook will show cost at 0.5x, 1x, 2x, and 5x expected traffic. Also show fallback to hosted for bursts and the unit economics.
[03:52] Carlos: Security questions — SSO/SAML and KMS integration are blockers for procurement. We need the SOC2 report and assurance around encryption-in-use. Is there an HSM pathway?
[04:05] Jordan: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II; will attach the cert. Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integration for dedicated and private deployments. For the dedicated pool, you can bring your own KMS keys; for fully air-gapped, there's an on-prem option.
[04:20] Aisha: timeline?
[04:22] Jordan: Typical onboarding for VPC + SSO is 2–4 weeks once legal and network allowlists are in place. HSM lane adds another 2 weeks. We'll share a checklist.
[04:32] Tara: Great. On procurement, finance needs the CRM deal ID and the draft contract terms.
[04:37] Jordan: I'll push a draft commercial appendix and the CRM deal ID into the doc we share.
[04:42] Carlos: About quality — the human eval was on 500 examples; can we expand to 2,000 before signoff? The variance matters.
[04:50] Priya: We can run the larger eval but it'll take a few days; compute cost estimate included.
[04:55] Aisha: Please do 2,000, and include the scoring rubric and inter-rater agreement.
[05:00] Priya: noted.
[05:02] Speaker 4: (mumbled)
[05:05] Jordan: So to recap technical asks: Redwood runs tunings on the 2.7B quantized variant with the adjusted settings, produce latency traces with VPC peering, and expand human eval to 2,000. Commercial asks: final cost runbook, sensitivity analysis, SOC2 and KMS/HSM checklist. Finance to confirm commit window.
[05:25] Tara: For NPV we'll need uplift assumptions. Can Redwood suggest conservative, base, and aggressive uplift scenarios?
[05:31] Jordan: Yes — we'll include conversion uplift scenarios tied to latency improvements and better personalization.
[05:36] Carlos: One more point — backup strategy if Dedicated capacity is constrained. Do you offer automatic fallback to compatible model variants in other regions?
[05:45] Priya: Yes, auto-fallback policies can route traffic to a lower-cost hosted variant or a nearby dedicated pool. We can instrument per-route fallbacks and also set percentage-based routing for gradual rollouts.
[05:58] Aisha: What's the monitoring story for regressions? We need alerting on quality regression and immediate rollback.
[06:05] Priya: Redwood Optimize includes eval-based regression alerts tied to prompt sets. We can set threshold-based alerts (e.g., >5% drop) and automatic rollback to previous model version.
[06:18] Carlos: Good. Any blockers from legal?
[06:21] Tara: Legal needs the data processing addendum and better-defined data residency terms.
[06:27] Jordan: We'll include the DPA draft and residency notes.
[06:30] Aisha: Ok — timeline: we aim to have signoff by 2026-01-22 and exec readout 2026-01-27. Does that work for Redwood?
[06:40] Jordan: Yes. We'll prioritize the quant benchmark and expanded eval this week.
[06:44] Devon: quick SRE note — can you provide temporary credentials for the test harness?
[06:48] Priya: We'll spin a short-lived key and put instructions in the runbook.
[06:52] Carlos: Thanks — that's it from my side.
[06:54] Jordan: Okay pulling together the final items — Priya will own the technical reruns, I will own commercial and security docs, Tara you'll own the finance inputs, Carlos final traffic slice and signoff.
[07:06] Aisha: Thanks everyone — excited to close this out.
[07:08] Jordan: Great — we'll share the deck + appendix by Monday the 19th and follow up with the readout invite. Meeting adjourned.
[07:15] (call ends)
